title: Complete Economics – GV Sir Headshot Series
source: GvKaksha / Eduquity Pattern – SSC CGL Mains/MTS/Delhi Police/GD/CHSL

subtopics.name: Founders and Key Personalities
content: John Maynard Keynes (1883-1946): founder of Keynesian economics, father of modern macroeconomics #imp
Adam Smith: called the 'father of economics' for theories on capitalism, free markets, and supply and demand #imp
P.V. Narasimha Rao: 'Father of Indian Economic Reforms'; 10th PM of India (1991-1996); launched free-market LPG reforms #imp

subtopics.name: Micro vs Macro Economics
content: Fundamental problem in economics is scarcity - limited resources vs unlimited wants, forcing choices on resource allocation #imp
Microeconomics studies individual parts (demand/supply, firm behavior); Macroeconomics studies the entire economy (GDP, national output, aggregate demand/supply)
Micro focuses on individual prices, wages, production; Macro focuses on general price level, national income, total employment
Micro aims for optimal resource allocation and profit/utility maximization; Macro seeks economic stability, growth, full employment
Closest link between micro and macro: General Equilibrium (simultaneous equilibrium in all markets) #imp

subtopics.name: Circular Flow and Sector Models
content: Circular Flow Model represents continuous flow of money among sectors: Household, Firms, Government, Foreign sector
Two-Sector Model equilibrium: S = I (Savings = Investment)
Three-Sector Model equilibrium: C + S + T = C + I + G (adds Government; Taxes = leakage, Govt expenditure = injection)
Four-Sector Model equilibrium: Y = C + I + G + (X-M) (adds Foreign sector; X-M = Net Exports) #imp
Exports > Imports leads to increase in National Income (injection); Imports > Exports leads to decrease (leakage)

subtopics.name: Types of Economies
content: Capitalist: private ownership, market-determined prices, profit motive
Socialist: public ownership, centrally planned prices, social welfare
Mixed: both ownerships, both pricing mechanisms #imp

subtopics.name: Factors of Production
content: Four Factors of Production: Land (payment=Rent), Labour (payment=Wage), Capital (payment=Interest), Entrepreneurship (payment=Profit) #imp
Types of Capital: Fixed, Working, Venture
Types of Labour: Unskilled, Semi-skilled, Skilled, Professional

subtopics.name: Sectors of Indian Economy
content: By activity: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Quaternary, Quinary; by work condition: Organised, Unorganised; by ownership: Public, Private
Primary Sector: directly uses natural resources (agriculture, mining, fishing, forestry, dairy)
Secondary Sector: transforms raw materials into finished goods (manufacturing, construction, electricity, gas, water supply)
Tertiary Sector: provides services (IT, banking, healthcare, transport, education) - largest contributor to India's GDP #imp
Economic liberalization (1991 reforms) removed/reduced government restrictions, affecting all three sectors and integrating domestic economy with world trade/capital flows
Code on Social Security 2020 extends social security to organised, unorganised, gig, and platform sector workers via EPFO, ESIC
Organised Sector: registered, follows labor laws, regular employment, PF/health insurance/pension benefits
Unorganised Sector: mostly unregistered, casual/seasonal employment, lacks social security benefits

subtopics.name: Types of Goods
content: By excludability/rivalry: Private Goods (rival+excludable, e.g. food), Public Goods (non-rival+non-excludable, e.g. national defense), Common Resources (non-excludable+rival, e.g. fish in ocean - tragedy of commons), Club Goods (excludable+non-rival, e.g. Netflix, toll roads) #imp
By income sensitivity: Normal Goods (demand rises with income), Inferior Goods (demand falls with income, e.g. instant noodles), Luxury Goods (demand rises more than proportionally to income)

By price/market behavior: Substitute Goods (Coke & Pepsi), Complementary Goods (car & petrol), Giffen Goods (rare inferior goods, demand rises with price), Veblen/Snob Goods (luxury goods, high price increases demand as status symbol) #imp

subtopics.name: Demand, Utility and Cost Concepts
content: Law of Demand: Quantity Demanded proportional to 1/Price; inverse relationship between demand and price, graphically shown via Demand Curve #imp
Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility: as consumption of a commodity increases, marginal utility from each successive unit decreases; MU becomes zero at Point of Satiety, can turn negative beyond that
Opportunity Cost: value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made - central to 'what to produce' decisions (Capital Goods vs Consumer Goods) #imp

Cost concepts: Explicit Costs (direct payments - wages, rent), Implicit Costs (value of self-owned resources), Total Cost = FC+VC, Average Cost = TC/Output, Marginal Cost (cost of one more unit), Social Cost (private + external costs like pollution)

subtopics.name: Brain Drain and Liquidity Trap
content: Brain drain in India driven by Push factors (low salaries, limited research funding, poor infrastructure) and Pull factors (better career growth, liberal societies abroad)
Liquidity Trap: a situation of very low interest rates where speculative demand for money becomes perfectly elastic; expansionary monetary policy fails to boost the economy #imp

subtopics.name: Sixth and Seventh Plans
content: Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85): Led by Indira Gandhi; focused on increasing national income, modernizing technology, reducing poverty/unemployment via TRYSEM (skill transfer), IRDP (seats), NREP (slack season employment), controlling population growth #imp
Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90): Led by Rajiv Gandhi; aimed at 'food, work and productivity' - accelerating food grain production, employment, productivity; focus on small and cottage industries

subtopics.name: Annual Plans and LPG Era
content: Annual Plans (1990-92): Eighth Plan was postponed by 2 years due to political instability; 1990-91 and 1991-92 treated as Annual Plans amid foreign exchange reserve crisis

Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97): Led by P.V. Narasimha Rao; launched Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation (LPG) reforms to tackle worsening balance of payments, rising debt, budget deficits, industrial recession, inflation #imp

Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002): Led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee; theme 'Growth With Social Justice & Equality'; focused on private sector (Indian & FDI) with State as facilitator in social sectors (education, health) and infrastructure

subtopics.name: Plan Failures
content: Third Five Year Plan failed due to war (1962, 1965), rupee devaluation, and food crisis #imp

subtopics.name: Industrial Policy Resolutions
content: Industrial Policy Resolution 1948 laid the foundation for a mixed economy approach in India, dividing industries into categories based on state involvement
Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 classified industries into Schedule A (exclusive state control), Schedule B (mixed public-private), Schedule C (private sector) #imp

subtopics.name: New Industrial Policy 1991
content: Industrial Policy 1991 (New Industrial Policy) introduced LPG reforms - delicensing of industries, abolition of MRTP restrictions, opening to foreign investment (FDI/FII), reduction of public sector reservation #imp

This chapter carries high weightage (47 questions) - covers Industrial Licensing Policy, MRTP Act, disinvestment policies, and Make in India initiatives (supplemented from general knowledge as PDF extract on this chapter was limited)

subtopics.name: Demand and Utility Curves
content: Demand Curve: graphical representation of the demand function; shows inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, holding other factors constant #imp
Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility Curve: Marginal Utility declines with each additional unit consumed, reaching zero at the Point of Satiety and turning negative beyond it

subtopics.name: Other Macroeconomic Curves
content: Curves chapter carries lower weightage (3 Q) - also includes Phillips Curve, Laffer Curve, and Kuznets Curve concepts relevant to macroeconomic policy analysis (supplemented from general knowledge)

subtopics.name: Base Year and GDP/GVA
content: India changed the base year for calculating national accounts from 2004-05 to 2011-12 (important fact) #imp
GVA (Gross Value Added) = GDP + Subsidies on products - Taxes on products
GDP = Sum total of Gross Value Added (GVA) of all firms in the economy

subtopics.name: Income Aggregates
content: Net National Income (NNI) = GDP - Depreciation
Personal Income (PI) = National Income + Transfer Payments - Corporate Retained Earnings - Income Tax - Social Security Tax #imp

Alternate formula: PI = National Income - Undistributed corporate profits - Social security payments - Corporate tax + Government transfer payments + Business transfer payments + Net interest paid by government
Disposable Personal Income (DPI) = Personal Income - Direct Taxes (or Personal Tax Payments - Non-tax payments)

subtopics.name: Propensities and Multiplier
content: Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) = Change in Consumption / Change in Income
Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) = 1 - MPC; therefore MPC + MPS = 1 #imp
Higher MPC leads to a greater Keynesian multiplier effect; lower MPC means lower multiplier impact
According to Keynes, expanded government spending is the most effective tool to revive the economy during a recession

subtopics.name: Sectoral Contribution to GDP
content: Services sector contributes most to India's GDP (Agriculture employs more than 50% of workforce but contributes less to GDP) #imp
Share of industry in India's GDP in 1950-51 was 13%

subtopics.name: Liquidity Trap and Fiscal Policy
content: Liquidity Trap: very low interest rate scenario where money demand becomes perfectly elastic; expansionary monetary policy fails to stimulate growth #imp
Fiscal Policy involves government revenue (taxes) and expenditure decisions to influence the economy

subtopics.name: Monetary Policy Tools
content: Monetary Policy is managed by RBI through tools like repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR to control money supply and inflation (supplemented from general knowledge) #imp
Expansionary fiscal/monetary policy is used during recession (increased govt spending, lower interest rates); contractionary policy used to control inflation

subtopics.name: Union Budget Basics
content: The Union Budget is presented by the Finance Minister, detailing government revenue and expenditure for the fiscal year
Budget includes Revenue Budget (Revenue receipts & expenditure) and Capital Budget (Capital receipts & expenditure)
Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - Total Revenue Receipts (excluding borrowings) #imp

subtopics.name: Kelkar Committee
content: Kelkar Committee (2002-03) reviewed fiscal reforms for Direct and Indirect taxes under chairmanship of Vijay Kelkar - recommended rationalized income tax slabs, reduced corporate tax, and comprehensive GST #imp

subtopics.name: Trade and Indirect Taxes
content: Customs duty is imposed on goods imported into and exported out of India
Tariff measures under trade policy include both export taxes and import taxes
Goods and Services Tax (GST) amalgamated a large number of central and state taxes and cesses #imp

subtopics.name: Tax Reform Committees
content: Tax Reforms Committee 1991 was chaired by Raja J. Chelliah #imp
Kelkar Committee (2002-03): recommended 20% tax rate up to Rs 4 lakh income, 30% above; increased exemption limit; reduced corporate tax to 30% (domestic)/35% (foreign); proposed comprehensive GST

subtopics.name: State-level and Other Taxes
content: Entertainment tax and Entry tax (now replaced by GST) were levied by State Governments, not Central Government
Wealth Tax is known as 'Paper tax' in India #imp

subtopics.name: Banking Structure
content: RBI is India's central bank, responsible for monetary policy, currency issuance, and banking regulation (supplemented from general knowledge) #imp
Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks, and Cooperative Banks form India's banking structure

subtopics.name: Insurance and Financial Inclusion
content: This chapter (20 Q) also covers Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), types of insurance (life, general), and financial inclusion schemes like Jan Dhan Yojana #imp

subtopics.name: Key Economic Committees
content: Kelkar Committee (2002-03): Reviewed direct and indirect tax reforms; chaired by Vijay Kelkar #imp
Tax Reforms Committee (1991): Chaired by Raja J. Chelliah
This chapter (4 Q) also includes other important economic committees like Narasimham Committee (banking reforms) and Chakravarty Committee (monetary policy), supplemented from general knowledge
